headline: Joe Mama Angie Daddy Hangs 178.8 on Long Live King Henry With Purdy's 33.75 Still on the Bench
meme_brief: A team wins by 60 points while also benching a 33-point quarterback performance, because when you're 10-1 apparently it doesn't matter who you start.
recap:
Joe Mama Angie Daddy's 178.8-117.95 win over Long Live King Henry, a 60.85-point margin, was the week's biggest blowout by a wide berth. Joe Burrow (28.9), Javonte Williams (24.6), Jahmyr Gibbs (27.8) and Travis Kelce (24.4) all started and delivered, and Brock Purdy added 33.75 points from the bench. Long Live King Henry got 35.9 from Jonah Coleman and 31.15 from Jared Goff and still lost by 60.

No game was close. The tightest finish was Broke Dak Mountain's 102.8-80.65 win over mikelanta, a 22.15-point margin, with Josh Allen's 20.2 leading Broke Dak Mountain and Caleb Williams' 23.15 leading mikelanta.

Dak to the Future beat Waffle House 144.15-121.45 behind a 52.15-point outing from Dak Prescott, the league's top individual score this week. Meredith's Fan Club handled Silverbacks 136.9-78.0, with Patrick Mahomes going for 37.2. Non Regulators beat demon44 by 39.4, and Screaming Eagles took down Pukachu Chews You 114.1-79.25 behind Cam Ward's 33.7 points, a free-agent pickup that paid off immediately.

Two bench decisions stood out as real misses, though neither cost a result. Dak to the Future started Jordyn Tyson (1.5 points) over Carnell Tate (15.8), a 14.3-point gap, and Meredith's Fan Club started DK Metcalf (0.7) over Xavier Worthy (11.8), an 11.1-point gap. Both teams won.
transaction_desk:
The week's most notable process story belongs to mikelanta, who ran four separate moves — Ryan Flournoy in for Geno Smith, the Jets defense in for J.J. McCarthy, Mike Gesicki in for Hunter Henry, then the Steelers defense in for the Jets — and made two waiver claims from the #9 slot, the Flournoy and Jets adds, and then dropped the Jets for the Steelers as a free agent later in the week. That is a defense slot churned twice in a single week.

Demon44's addition of Seth McGowan is a sensible depth move given the listed handcuff relationship to Jonathan Taylor, even though it cost a mid-tier #8 priority slot — that's exactly the kind of injury insurance pickup worth making regardless of immediate production. Silverbacks' pickup of Michael Mayer barely registers as a cost since their priority was already next-to-last at #11. Pukachu Chews You spent a #6 priority on Bo Nix and got an immediate 17.75 points in his debut — a reasonable swing that paid off fast, though the later waiver claim on Woody Marks, listed at the same #6 slot, scored nothing.

On the results side, the Dallas Cowboys defense (picked up by Dak to the Future back in week 7 for zero cost) has delivered 22.0 cumulative points for nothing spent, and Antonio Williams has put up 40.8 points since demon44 added him for free in week 8. Those are the quiet value plays sitting underneath this week's bigger headlines. Joe Mama Angie Daddy, meanwhile, continues picking at the waiver wire with uncontested moves (Tyler Goodson, Kendre Miller, Jordan Addison in sequence, the last two essentially canceling out) while sitting at 10-1 — tinkering at the margins of a team that clearly doesn't need much help.

standings_narrative:
The sixth and final playoff seed is still Long Live King Henry's to lose, but barely. The sixth-seed race summary has Long Live King Henry holding the spot with 1318.99 season points, with Pukachu Chews You trailing by just 2.44 points, mikelanta down 27.44, and Screaming Eagles down 38.54. A gap of 2.44 points is about as tight as this kind of race gets, and it's the headline of the playoff picture right now even though Long Live King Henry sits at 4-7.

The top of the bracket is settled by record for now: Joe Mama Angie Daddy (10-1), Non Regulators (7-4), and Broke Dak Mountain (7-4) hold the three division-winner seeds. Meredith's Fan Club (7-4) and Dak to the Future (6-5) occupy the next-best-record seeds 4 and 5. Everything below that is about point totals, not wins, which is why Pukachu Chews You at 5-6 is realistically one good week away from leapfrogging a 4-7 team into the final playoff spot.
look_ahead:
Next week, Non Regulators (7-4) face mikelanta (4-7) in a game Non Regulators should expect to control given the records involved. Joe Mama Angie Daddy (10-1) draws Dak to the Future (6-5), a measuring-stick matchup between the league's best record and a team still fighting for playoff positioning. Broke Dak Mountain (7-4) hosts demon44 (4-7), and Waffle House (1-10) faces Long Live King Henry (4-7) in a game that matters a great deal to Long Live King Henry's grip on the sixth seed.

Silverbacks (5-6) and Pukachu Chews You (5-6) meet directly, with Pukachu Chews You sitting just 2.44 points back of the final playoff spot — a strong week here would do real work in that race. Meredith's Fan Club (7-4) closes out the slate against Screaming Eagles (6-5), both teams jockeying for playoff position from different angles.
